html:
The constitution of 1964 turned the Kingdom of Afghanistan into a constitutional monarchy, with an elected parliament and equal rights for men and women, including the vote for women.

King Mohammad Zahir Shah had it drafted after he removed his powerful cousin, Prime Minister Mohammed Daoud Khan, in 1963. A grand council of elders, a loya jirga, approved it. One clause barred members of the royal family from party politics and high office, aimed squarely at Daoud.

The decade that followed is called the "New Democracy". Elections were held, newspapers multiplied and Kabul University grew into a centre of student politics, both communist and Islamist. But the king never signed the law that would have allowed political parties, and governments were weak. In 1973 Daoud seized power in a coup and declared a republic, ending the monarchy. A cycle of coups and war followed, leading to the Soviet invasion of 1979.
sum: The constitution of 1964 turned the Kingdom of Afghanistan into a constitutional monarchy, with an elected parliament and equal rights for men and women, including the vote for women.
